results.name: hud_counter_get_value
results.evidence: reads a per-player counter struct at DAT_006b3a40 (active flag +0x487, raw value +0x47c, mode flag +0x486, base +0x478) and, unless the raw value is the 0xffff sentinel (returns -1), optionally adjusts it against the current game tick at DAT_006f1d6c+0xc; consumed by hud_counter_update and hud_chat_to_network before their per-type jump tables
results.summary: Computes the current display value of a HUD numeric counter widget, returning -1 when the counter holds the 'no value' sentinel.

results.name: hud_counter_update
results.evidence: renamed from the chimera__ hint; reads the same counter struct as hud_counter_get_value, checks a local-player-indexed globals table at DAT_00746fa0 (+0x140/+0x144) for a valid handle at +0xbc, and then dispatches through the function-pointer table PTR_LAB_004adfa0 indexed by the counter-type byte at +0x484
results.summary: Per-frame update entry point for a local player's HUD counter widget: fetches its value then dispatches to a per-counter-type handler via a jump table.

results.name: hud_chat_to_network
results.evidence: structurally near-identical to hud_counter_update (same counter struct, same DAT_00746fa0 lookup, same PTR_LAB_004adfa0 jump table indexed by the same sVar1), but additionally reads a byte at tag+0x11 and re-encodes it via FUN_006391b4 before the dispatch; has 0 direct callers so it is itself one of the entries reached only through that jump table
results.summary: One of the per-type handlers reached through the HUD counter's jump table; re-encodes an extra tag-derived byte alongside the counter value before falling into the same per-type dispatch as hud_counter_update (existing name kept but not strongly confirmed to be about network chat specifically).

results.name: hud_set_pointed_player_name
results.evidence: given a local-player index (param_1) and a network-player index (in_AX), stores a pointer into a 0x40-byte-stride name-table entry (base at DAT_0071941c+0xfc's referenced table) into the per-player struct's +0x454 field and sets a validity flag at +0x458, guarded by an activity flag at DAT_00719420+1
results.summary: Records (or clears) which network player's name-table entry a local player's HUD widget is currently pointing at.

results.name: hud_message_set_argument_value
results.evidence: writes a 4-byte value (param_1) into a per-player argument slot array at +0x434 indexed by an implicit register (unaff_SI) and clears the corresponding bit in a type bitmask at +0x459, guarded by the +0x458 active flag and +0x454 non-null pointer set by hud_set_pointed_player_name
results.summary: Stores a raw numeric substitution argument for the local player's current HUD action/message text and marks that argument slot as non-string.

results.name: hud_message_set_argument_string
results.evidence: mirrors hud_message_set_argument_value's guard conditions but writes a 2-byte value plus a 1-byte value (param_1/param_2) into the same +0x434 argument array and instead SETS the corresponding bit in the +0x459 bitmask
results.summary: Stores a short+byte substitution argument (e.g. a string id) for the local player's current HUD action/message text and marks that argument slot as a string.

results.name: hud_prompt_set_active
results.evidence: toggles the per-player struct's +0x458 active flag to unaff_BL, ORs a 'changed' bit into +0x45e when the state differs from before, clears the +0x454 pointer, and when activating (unaff_BL != 0) blanks the +0x230 wide-char text buffer via _wcsncpy; +0x230 is the same buffer later checked by hud_messaging_update as one of the conditions for drawing the message overlay
results.summary: Enables or disables the local player's HUD action-prompt widget (the on-screen text tied to the +0x230 buffer), clearing its text when turned on.

results.name: hud_message_add
results.evidence: renamed from the chimera__ hint; takes a local-player index (in_AX) and a wide string (param_1), finds a free/oldest message slot via hud_message_find_slot, copies up to 63 wide chars into it, stamps it with the current game tick (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc), assigns it an increasing per-player sequence number from +0x465, and marks the per-player 'dirty' flag at +0x45e
results.summary: Adds a new timestamped text message into the local player's HUD message slot array, evicting the oldest/least-relevant slot if needed.

results.name: hud_item_pickup_check
results.evidence: iterates a datum array via data_iterator_next looking for an entry whose type field (psVar2[0x184]) selects among a small set of item categories (2,3,5), calling different per-category handlers, and for category 2 sets flag bit 0x10 on the object returned by object_try_and_get(1) and ends by calling FUN_00543dd0(1.0f) which resembles a play-sound call
results.summary: Scans nearby pickup-able items for the local player and, depending on item category, flags the referenced object and/or triggers a HUD pickup notification/sound.

results.name: hud_message_send
results.evidence: if network play is active (DAT_00719720 != 0) encodes a type-6 payload via message_delta_encode_message and forwards it with network_session_send_to_machine; otherwise falls back to calling hud_message_apply_local directly
results.summary: Sends a HUD message/counter update over the network when playing multiplayer, or applies it locally otherwise.

results.name: hud_message_apply_local
results.evidence: local (non-networked) counterpart used by hud_message_send: looks up a message slot via hud_message_find_slot, bumps a duration/count field at +0x88 by param_1, stamps the slot with the current game tick from DAT_006f1d6c+0xc, and marks the per-player sequence id from +0x465
results.summary: Applies a HUD message/counter increment directly to the local player's message slot without going over the network.

results.name: hud_message_find_slot
results.evidence: scans up to 4 fixed-size (0x8c-byte) message slots at param_1, matching one whose stored source id (offset 0x84) and type byte (offset 0x8a) equal the caller's implicit unaff_ESI/param_2, else returns the slot with the lowest 'timestamp' field (offset 0)
results.summary: Finds an existing HUD message slot for a given source/type, or otherwise the oldest slot available for reuse.

results.name: hud_message_compare
results.evidence: pure comparator with clean stack parameters (no register-only inputs): compares two message-slot pointers first by their offset-0 timestamp field, then by offset 0x84 (source id), then by the offset 0x83 priority byte -- consistent with being the qsort() callback used by hud_messaging_update
results.summary: Ordering comparator for sorting HUD message slots by timestamp, then source id, then priority.

results.name: hud_messaging_update
results.evidence: matches a cea-pdb string hint via the referenced string '<no button icon>'; reads the per-player messaging struct (counter sub-fields +0x470/+0x474, action-prompt fields +0x458/+0x454/+0x230), builds render data and calls chimera__draw_16_bit_text (renamed target) and _qsort to order pending HUD messages
results.summary: Per-frame update that assembles and draws the local player's HUD counter, action-prompt, and queued text messages.

results.name: hud_widget_find_by_name
results.evidence: linearly scans a 0x68-byte-stride name table (count/pointer at DAT_0071941c+0x160/+0x164) comparing each entry's leading string against an implicit caller-supplied string (unaff_EDI) with __stricmp, returning the matching index or -1
results.summary: Case-insensitive lookup of a named entry's index within a small interface-related name table.

results.name: hud_waypoint_set
results.evidence: looks up a category via the players data table (DAT_0087a480), and when it is 0, scans up to 4 slots of 0xc bytes each in the DAT_006b3a44 table (distinct from the DAT_006b3a40 message struct) keyed by a 4-bit id (in_DX) and a source id (unaff_EBX), overwriting a matching slot or the first free (-1) one with param_1/param_2
results.summary: Stores or updates one entry of a small (4-slot) per-object waypoint/marker table used by the HUD navigation-arrow system.

results.name: hud_waypoint_set_by_type
results.evidence: iterates a datum array via data_iterator_next, calling hud_waypoint_set for every entry whose type field at offset 0x20 matches param_2
results.summary: Applies hud_waypoint_set to every active datum of a given type, e.g. to add/refresh waypoint markers for all objects of that category.

results.name: hud_waypoint_clear
results.evidence: mirror of hud_waypoint_set: scans the same DAT_006b3a44 4-slot table for the entry matching (unaff_SI, unaff_EDI) and, if found, resets its id fields to 0xffff/0xffff, marking the slot free
results.summary: Removes one entry from the per-object waypoint/marker table.

results.name: hud_waypoint_clear_by_type
results.evidence: iterates a datum array via data_iterator_next calling hud_waypoint_clear for every entry whose type field at offset 0x20 equals param_1
results.summary: Clears waypoint/marker table entries for every active datum of a given type.

results.name: hud_waypoint_update_all_players
results.evidence: standard local-player iteration idiom over DAT_0087a478 (start at 0, loop while a next player exists) calling hud_waypoint_update_for_player for each
results.summary: Runs the per-player waypoint/marker update for every active local player.

results.name: hud_waypoint_update_for_player
results.evidence: indexes the DAT_006b3a44 4-slot waypoint table for the given player, calls object_try_and_get and FUN_004f6080 (tag lookup style call with &DAT_0066bfa0), and updates a nibble field packing a computed flag from hud_waypoint_get_type_flags for each of the 4 slots
results.summary: Refreshes each of a local player's active waypoint/marker slots for the current frame.

results.name: hud_waypoint_get_type_flags
results.evidence: calls FUN_00505880 with a fixed magic id (0xc2ad), consistent with the codebase's tag/setting-lookup-by-hash pattern, then compares two of its output fields against param_1, returning 2 or 0
results.summary: Looks up a small type/flag value (via a hashed setting lookup) used to classify a waypoint/marker entry.

results.name: hud_waypoint_draw
results.evidence: projects a 3D position (in_EAX) relative to unit_get_camera_position() and matrix4x3_transform_point() into screen space, computes an off-screen bearing angle via fpatan when the target falls outside the frustum, and calls FUN_004ab8d0/FUN_004acbb0-family meter/icon drawing helpers -- the classic on-screen 'off-screen target' navigation-arrow calculation
results.summary: Computes screen position (or clamped edge-of-screen bearing arrow) for a single HUD waypoint marker and draws its icon.

results.name: hud_waypoint_draw_all
results.evidence: clean stack-only parameter (no register-only inputs); for a given local player index (param_1) iterates the 4 DAT_006b3a44 waypoint slots and calls hud_waypoint_draw for each valid one, resolving its 3D anchor position either from an object via object_try_and_get or a cached one via FUN_00462230
results.summary: Draws all of a local player's active waypoint/navigation-arrow markers for the current frame.

results.name: hud_interface_sync_looping_sounds
results.evidence: all parameters are clean stack values (no register-only inputs); param_2 is used as a TagReflexive-style {count, pointer} pair, and the code special-cases entries whose tag group fourCC equals 0x6c736e64 ('lsnd' = looping_sound) calling datum_new()/FUN_00549af0 (start) and FUN_00549ee0 (stop) to keep active sound datums in sync with a tag block of sound references and a bitmask of active flags
results.prototype: void __cdecl hud_interface_sync_looping_sounds(unsigned int active_mask, TagReflexive *sound_block, int *sound_datum_indices, unsigned short *active_flags)
results.summary: Starts, stops, or updates the looping sound datums referenced by a hud_interface tag block so they match the caller-supplied active-flag bitmask.

results.name: hud_meter_update_flags
results.evidence: reads a per-object shield/health pair at offsets 0x38/0x39 (float words) of the object returned by object_try_and_get(3) -- the same 0xe0/0xe4 byte offsets used for shield/health in hud_meter_update_value -- and derives a bitmask of blink/low/empty flags passed into hud_interface_sync_looping_sounds as the active-sound mask; sets pfVar8[7] to -NaN (a hidden-meter sentinel) when the object is invulnerable or already zero
results.summary: Computes the blink/low-health/empty state flags for a local player's shield or health meter and drives its associated warning sounds.

results.name: hud_meter_update_all_players
results.evidence: standard local-player iteration idiom over DAT_0087a478 calling hud_meter_update_value for each active local player
results.summary: Runs the per-player shield/health meter smoothing update for every active local player.

results.name: hud_meter_update_value
results.evidence: reads an object's current/max values from offsets 0xe0/0xe4 (matching the shield/health float offsets also used by hud_meter_update_flags), smooths the displayed meter value in the DAT_0071942c array toward it at a fixed rate of 0.033333335 (1/30 s), and conditionally calls hud_meter_update_flags when a HUD state-change flag (DAT_006f187c+9) is set
results.summary: Per-frame smoothing/animation of a local player's displayed shield or health meter value toward the unit's actual current value.

results.name: hud_render_unit_interface
results.evidence: matches a cea-pdb string hint via the referenced bitmap strings 'ui\shell\bitmaps\team_icon_ctf/king/oddball/race/slayer' and 'team_background'; calls tag_lookup, game_engine_get_player_color, and object_try_and_get while building the per-unit HUD render state
results.summary: Builds and draws the on-screen weapon/vehicle HUD interface (crosshairs, meters, team icon) for the local player's controlled unit.

results.name: hud_directional_ping_update
results.evidence: calls FUN_00457220 to populate a 4-entry validity/intensity array, then for each of 4 fixed angles (0, pi/2, 0, 3pi/2 via the literals 0x40490fdb/0x3fc90fdb/0/0x4096cbe4) computes an edge-of-screen position offset by the viewport center (DAT_007c3140) and, if measurable via FUN_004ab8d0, draws an icon via FUN_004acbb0
results.summary: Draws up to four fixed-direction on-screen indicator icons (e.g. edge-of-screen pings) around the viewport border.

results.name: hud_meter_apply_damage_prediction
results.evidence: looks up a player-table entry for an encoded object id (in_ECX) via DAT_0087a480 to get a local-player index, then subtracts param_1 directly from that player's cached meter value in the DAT_0071942c array (the same array smoothed by hud_meter_update_value)
results.summary: Immediately subtracts a damage amount from a local player's cached shield/health meter display, ahead of the next authoritative object-state update.

results.name: hud_weapon_interface_resolve_all_players
results.evidence: clean niladic function (no register-only inputs); for each local player, resolves their controlled unit's active weapon/vehicle hud_interface tag (falling back through a parent-seat check and unit_get_weapon_object_index-style logic via FUN_0056d990) and caches the result per-player at DAT_00719430+idx*0x28
results.summary: For every local player, determines which weapon/vehicle hud_interface tag currently applies to their unit and caches it for later meter updates.

results.name: hud_weapon_interface_update_meters
results.evidence: walks a chain of up to 16 parent hud_interface tag references, accumulates a bitmask of active meter types from each tag's offset 0x9c field, then dispatches through the PTR_LAB_004b1dc8 function-pointer table once per set bit -- mirroring the per-type dispatch pattern seen in hud_counter_update
results.summary: Updates every active meter/crosshair element of a unit's weapon hud_interface by dispatching to a per-meter-type handler table.

results.name: hud_update_spectated_unit_interface
results.evidence: renamed from the chimera__ hint; given an object (param_1), resolves its weapon hud_interface the same way as hud_weapon_interface_resolve_all_players (parent-seat fallback via FUN_0056d990, unit_get_weapon_object_index) and then calls hud_weapon_meters_update / hud_weapon_interface_build_elements to populate its meters, caching the result in the same DAT_00719430 table used for local players
results.summary: Resolves and updates the weapon HUD interface state for an arbitrary (e.g. spectated/followed) unit rather than only the local player's own unit.

results.name: hud_weapon_interface_update
results.evidence: builds packed bitfields describing a weapon's crosshair/meter layout from up to three optional parameter blocks (param_5/6/7) or, when absent, from the unit's own weapon tag data (in_EAX+0x12 vs tag+0x14); calls unit_get_camera_position and recurses into itself, consistent with handling a second (offhand/dual-wield) weapon
results.summary: Computes the crosshair/meter bitfield state for one of a unit's weapons, recursing once to also handle a secondary (dual-wielded) weapon.

results.name: hud_weapon_meters_update
results.evidence: clean stack-only parameters (no register-only inputs); looks up the object at param_2 in the objects table, reads its current weapon-index field (offset 0x31c), and for the corresponding weapon hud_interface tag calls FUN_004ac6f0 twice (for the primary offset +0x24 and secondary trigger offset +0x8c), plus unit_get_current_grenade_index/unit_get_grenade_count feeding a grenade-count meter update (FUN_004ac0b0) and another meter update at tag offset +0x14c
results.prototype: void __cdecl hud_weapon_meters_update(int slot_index, unsigned int object_id)
results.summary: Updates a unit's ammo, dual-trigger, and grenade-count HUD meters from its current weapon and grenade state.

results.name: hud_weapon_interface_build_elements
results.evidence: pure leaf function (no callees) that walks a weapon tag's hud_interface element sub-blocks (0x6c-byte stride, count field +0x1a) and, per element type (switch on sVar3), packs meter/crosshair render parameters (color at +0x24, scale +0x46, flags +0x48) into an output buffer -- used by hud_update_spectated_unit_interface
results.summary: Builds the list of renderable crosshair/meter element parameters from a weapon's hud_interface tag data.

results.name: hud_screen_indicator_draw
results.evidence: Ghidra failed to decompile this function ('Cannot properly adjust input varnodes'), so behavior is inferred only from context: its globals overlap the viewport-offset fields (DAT_007c3140/007c3144) used elsewhere for screen-space drawing, and its callees are FUN_00444550 (a boolean gate used elsewhere to check local-player screen visibility) and FUN_004acad0 (an icon/meter drawing helper family)
results.summary: Likely draws a screen-space HUD indicator icon guarded by a visibility check, but the exact behavior could not be recovered from the decompiler output.

results.name: blip_type_get
results.evidence: matches a cea-pdb string hint ('blip_type_get') via the referenced string 'c_dropship'; compares the local player's team (via FUN_00474db0, a sibling of local_player_to_player_index) against param_1, then checks a vehicle object's seat fields (+0xc9/+0xca) and, for a vehicle with tag name 'c_dropship', returns a distinct code -- returning one of 6 categories (own-team, no-compare-unit, no-local-unit, generic-vehicle, dropship, invalid)
results.summary: Classifies an object (relative to the local player) into a small set of radar/HUD blip categories: friendly, vehicle, dropship, or invalid/unavailable.

results.name: blip_type_get_and_subtype
results.evidence: calls blip_type_get and stores its result, then for a valid object reads a further short field at tag offset 0x298 (clamped to 0-2) as a secondary subtype byte
results.summary: Fills in a blip record's primary type (via blip_type_get) and a secondary subtype code for an object.

results.name: motion_sensor_reset
results.evidence: clean niladic function; zeroes the entire DAT_00719438 motion-sensor blip array and then writes the sentinel value 6 (the same 'empty' marker checked/written by motion_sensor_update_for_player) into every one of the 10 history frames' 0x10 blip-type slots
results.summary: Clears the motion sensor's blip history buffer, marking every history-frame slot as empty.

results.name: motion_sensor_object_is_detected
results.evidence: checks an object's flag word (+0x208) and category byte (+0x28d), computes squared distance to the local player's position against the motion-sensor radius constant at DAT_0071941c+0x2d4, and factors in a 'detect stationary objects' toggle (DAT_00710300), returning a packed detected/visible byte result
results.summary: Determines whether a given object should currently register as a blip on the local player's motion sensor.

results.name: motion_sensor_draw_blip
results.evidence: rotates a relative object position by the object's facing angle (offset 0x7c) via fsin/fcos, compares the squared distance to the motion-sensor radius constant at DAT_0071941c+0x2d0, and if within range calls FUN_0052bad0 with a computed intensity -- consistent with plotting one blip on the circular motion-sensor display
results.summary: Plots a single detected object as a blip on the motion sensor display, oriented relative to the viewer's facing.

results.name: motion_sensor_update
results.evidence: renamed from the chimera__ hint; computes a FOV-based scale factor via FUN_00628cca into DAT_0071943c, resets each local player's current motion-sensor history frame using the same value 6 sentinel written by motion_sensor_reset, then iterates all objects via object_iterator_next calling motion_sensor_object_is_detected-style logic for each
results.summary: Per-frame update of the motion sensor: advances the history ring buffer and re-scans all objects for detection against each local player.

results.name: motion_sensor_update_for_player
results.evidence: for a single local player (param_1), re-tests each of the 16 blip slots in the current history frame against motion_sensor_object_is_detected-style distance checks, clearing (writing the value 6 sentinel) any blip that has moved out of the motion-sensor radius (DAT_0071941c+0x2d0) or is otherwise invalid, and refreshes positions for the ones that remain
results.summary: Refreshes one local player's motion sensor blip slots for the current frame, dropping blips that have left detection range.

results.name: motion_sensor_render
results.evidence: iterates the last 10 history frames for a given screen quadrant/player context (in_CX), skipping known-empty (value 6) or filtered blip types depending on DAT_006f1d20/DAT_006f1cc0 flags, and calls motion_sensor_draw_blip for each remaining entry with a fading intensity that decreases with frame age
results.summary: Draws the motion sensor display for a local player by rendering each historical blip with age-based fading.

results.name: controls_value_is_reserved
results.evidence: linearly scans the fixed int array DAT_0065c15c..DAT_0065c180 for a value equal to the implicit register input (in_EDX), returning 0 (found/reserved) or 1 (not found); used by controls_get_next_available_action to skip already-used ids while building the key-binding action list
results.summary: Checks whether a given action/id value is present in the reserved-values table used by the controls-binding UI.

results.name: controls_get_next_available_action
results.evidence: repeatedly calls an enumerator (FUN_0053aa20) to advance through candidate action ids, using controls_value_is_reserved to skip reserved ones, and supports a two-pass mode (param_1) that first excludes and then allows previously-seen ids -- consistent with building the assignable-actions list in the control-binding menu
results.summary: Enumerates the next assignable control-binding action, skipping values already reserved or already listed.

results.name: controls_get_action_name
results.evidence: calls controls_get_next_available_action(1) then FUN_0048c7f0 (a string-id-to-text resolver elsewhere in this module) to fill DAT_006b3d48, falling back to the literal string '???' via _wcscpy when nothing was resolved
results.summary: Returns the localized display name for a control-binding action, or '???' if none is available.

results.name: controls_ui_update_binding_labels
results.evidence: references the string '?forward' (a default/placeholder action name) and manipulates a chain of UI widget nodes (next/child pointers at +0x2c/+0x34, text pointer at +0x3c, enabled/dim flags at +0x10/+0x12/+0x24) using controls_get_action_name to set each widget's label text based on whether a binding exists in the DAT_00692ff8/DAT_00692ffc tables
results.summary: Updates the text and enabled/dimmed state of the control-binding list widgets for one input mapping row.

results.name: controls_ui_refresh_binding_list
results.evidence: walks an 8-entry linked widget chain (offsets +0x30/+0x38/+0x2c matching a doubly-linked UI list), tracking the currently focused item against DAT_006953e8 and calling controls_ui_update_binding_labels for each
results.summary: Refreshes every visible row of the control-binding list widget, tracking which row currently has focus.

results.name: controls_add_device_label
results.evidence: clean stack-only parameters; scans the DAT_006932e8 label table for the first empty (zero) 0x210-byte-stride slot, copies param_1 into it via _wcsncpy and stores param_2 alongside, and increments the device count at DAT_00719440
results.summary: Registers a new named input-device entry in the controls-menu device label table.

results.name: controls_build_device_label_table
results.evidence: references the tag path 'ui\shell\...\controls_setup\controls_device_labels' via tag_lookup and calls controls_add_device_label once for a default entry and then for up to 4 connected devices read from the tag's string-list block
results.summary: Builds the controls-menu's device name table from the controls_device_labels tag and the currently connected input devices.

results.name: controls_apply_preset
results.evidence: branches on a UI-mode flag (DAT_00719445) and a device-count field; when applying a preset it calls FUN_00490110 with fixed 32-bit magic constants (resembling a tag/GUID lookup) to fetch preset binding data, copying it into the DAT_00714fb4.. binding table, or otherwise calls FUN_0053b500(index) to apply one of five stock control schemes
results.summary: Applies a stock or looked-up control-binding preset to the current input configuration.

results.name: controls_binding_is_default
results.evidence: tests bit 0 or bit 1 (selected by in_ECX) of the per-action byte array &DAT_00692ffc, the same table whose bits controls_ui_update_binding_labels reads to decide whether a custom binding exists
results.summary: Returns whether a given input's primary or secondary binding is still at its default (unmodified) value.

results.name: controls_reset_binding
results.evidence: references the '?forward' placeholder string; when the binding is already default (via the same bit tests as controls_binding_is_default) it exits early, otherwise clears matching entries from the DAT_007127d4 current-bindings table or, for the alternate device-label path, clears entries in a device-scoped table computed the same way as in controls_build_device_label_table (DAT_00714e7c/DAT_00714e80)
results.summary: Clears a single control binding back to its unbound/default state.

results.name: controls_ui_update_focused_binding
results.evidence: references the '?forward' placeholder string; manages the currently-focused binding row (DAT_006953e8), copies its action name via controls_get_action_name into an allocated buffer, calls controls_ui_refresh_binding_list's helper (FUN_004b4790) for state, and special-cases a scancode of 0x1d (Ctrl) to call controls_reset_binding as a 'clear binding' shortcut
results.summary: Handles input on the currently focused control-binding row, including looking up its display name and a keyboard shortcut to clear it.

results.name: controls_ui_toggle_binding_widgets
results.evidence: toggles the enabled/dimmed state of two sibling binding-row widgets based on a boolean parameter and a connected-device-count check (DAT_00714e7c), and reads per-device axis/button limit bytes from DAT_007157d3/DAT_007157d7 to clamp a displayed index
results.summary: Enables or disables a pair of control-binding row widgets depending on whether a compatible input device is connected.

results.name: controls_ui_get_widget_references
results.evidence: pure pointer-chasing helper with no globals or callees: walks a fixed sequence of widget next/child pointers (offsets +0x2c/+0x34) to populate a caller-supplied array of 17 widget references, matching the fixed layout of the controls-binding menu
results.summary: Collects pointers to a fixed set of controls-menu widget nodes for later use by the binding-list update code.

results.name: controls_ui_populate_device_names
results.evidence: calls controls_ui_get_widget_references, then fills two widget lists (bound at DAT_006b53d8/DAT_006b42d8) with device name strings up to the connected counts DAT_00719448/DAT_0071944c, writing '---' or '' placeholders and dimming the widget for entries beyond the connected count
results.summary: Populates the controls menu's device-selection widget lists with the names of connected input devices, padding unused entries with placeholders.
